speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your age and exactly when you first noticed these skin lesions appearing? Also, have you experienced any fever, itching, or pain associated with them?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of these papules, specifically if they have a central dimple or are filled with clear fluid? I would also like to know if the lesions are spreading to other areas of the body or if the child has had any contact with a person who has molluscum contagiosum.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic description of umbilicated, pearly papules and the daycare exposure, I am fairly confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum.
